codex-notify 1.0.1 reduces internal Codex activity appearing in Slack and adds
dependency security checks to the development workflow.

## Fixes

- Suppress the known Codex task-title and Composer Predictions instruction
  templates and their internal responses in Hook normal mode and log-tail mode.
- Preserve an existing Slack conversation thread during internal-request
  suppression and resume notifications on the next ordinary user prompt.
- Keep initial-prompt suppression active when a log session ID becomes known,
  without suppressing other sessions.

## Development and security

- Audit locked gems and Bundler before CI tests and package verification,
  daily at 09:17 Japan time, and on manual dispatch. Pull requests also run
  GitHub Dependency Review.
- Require advisory database refreshes and detect vulnerabilities even when
  project advisory ignore entries are present.
- Use Ruby 4.0.7 for preferred local development and CI/release jobs.

## Compatibility

- Ruby 3.4 or newer remains supported. Installed gems have no new runtime
  dependencies, and existing configuration and Hook payloads remain compatible.
- Ordinary requests, quoted internal templates, and standalone suggestion or
  title JSON remain eligible for notification. Unknown or changed internal
  templates are not suppressed automatically. Hook debug mode retains visibility
  of internal requests and responses.
- No configuration migration is required. Update the installed gem with
  `gem update codex-notify` and restart any running log-tail monitor.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/koichiro/codex-notify/blob/v1.0.1/CHANGELOG.md)
and the [README](https://github.com/koichiro/codex-notify/blob/v1.0.1/README.md)
for matching details and audit requirements.
